chapter: Career overview and the Lunceford quarrel
title: Buying a full Leedy drum set for the Cotton Club
summary: Crawford explains the quarrel with Lunceford: told to have drums for the Cotton Club, he paid about $1,600 for a set on $60 a week while Lunceford bought no uniforms.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Well, me, that man inspired me so much that I didn't want to be nothing but a drummer. I've got some more to tell you later years (inaudible). Why, Lunceford and I had a big argument. We were in some theater playing with Bill Robinson Enwright. This was after we had got to New York and were in the Cotton Club. And we got in a heck of an argument, heated argument. Of course, Lunceford was such a gentleman, he wouldn't dare fight or nothing like that, no -- I was quarterback on his football team and half -- halfback in Memphis at Manassas High School where he was a physical ed. man. He was a great athlete and a great gentleman. I don't know why I got so angry with Lunceford. On second thought I do know why, because Lunceford didn't ever buy his band's uniforms.

Cab Calloway, Duke Ellington and the big bands like that -- well, Cab Calloway and Duke Ellington I knew. On top of that, Stanley, I went in behind Cab Calloway, Lunceford's band did, while Sammy Greer -- you know him -- he was playing drums for Duke Ellington, and all the drummers that appeared

in the Cotton Club with those bands had fabulous drum outfits, gongs, chimes, vibraphones, timpanies, all kind of drums hanging around. It was a beautiful setting for those bands. Well, Stocks told Harold Oxley and Jimmie Lunsford, now, your drummer got to have some drums up there. I was sitting up there with a bass drum and one cymbal. He said, no, we used to seeing drums in here, make a beautiful setting for the band.

So went to work and I, you know, I took it upon myself to go and buy a whole complete set of Leedy drums like Sonny Greer and Manzie and Cab, like what they had, and they did set the band off. It looked beautiful, took me a day to set them up.

And so I had to pay for them. I think it was around about 1,600.00. Now, I'm making about $60.00 a week, and I got pretty burned up about that, plus Lunsford never bought any uniforms or paid for the uniforms that we wore in his band to make his band impressive.
